member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Adoption.AdoptCommand
member.summary: lockflight adopt plan|apply|undo: takes over an existing Claude Code and Spec Kit setup. plan only reads and writes .lockflight/adopt/plan.md; apply and undo are human decisions, refused inside a Claude Code session. Undo reverts what apply changed, and keeps files changed since (unless forced).

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Adoption.AdoptionBackup
member.summary: What adoption may change, archived before apply under .lockflight/backup/<id>.tar.gz (git-ignored local state): CLAUDE.md, lockflight.yaml, the adopted-features baseline, and the files of .claude/ (except settings.local.json, which adoption never touches and which may hold secrets, and worktrees/, which holds other sessions' checkouts), .specify/ and specs/. member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Adoption.GuardPatterns
member.summary: The path patterns of a shell guard script, as Lockflight globs: its case arms (*docker-compose.override.yml*|*"/Contracts/"*), or exact names such as ".env")) and its [[ "$FILE" == *"name" ]] tests. A file name becomes **/name, a path fragment between slashes becomes **/fragment/**. A pattern without a wildcard counts only when it looks like a path (it has a '.' or a '/'), so arms that match tool names (Edit|Write)) are not mistaken for files. An arm or test that lets the call through (an empty arm, or one with exit 0) is an allow-list entry, not a guarded path: a secrets scanner that allows secrets in .env does not protect .env. Patterns that are not plain (variables, character classes) are left out — the hook still guards them.

member.summary: What runs when a test holds: up to fi for if … then, else the rest of the line (&& exit 0).

○ Match ')'.
○ "body" capture group.

○ Match the string ";;".
○ Match any character.
○ Match the string ";;".

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Adoption.HookClassifier
member.summary: Decides what adoption does with a hook, from its event, matcher and script text (keep and flag; replace nothing automatically). A PreToolUse write guard that blocks by path patterns gets those patterns added to protected:; a hook that rewrites files after an edit, or builds at Stop, is flagged; everything else is kept as the team's own control. A command that names $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR without quotes is flagged too (a guard keeps its paths): in a project whose path has a space it never runs, and Claude Code reports that only as a non-blocking error.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Adoption.SpecKitMerge
member.summary: Upgrades the Spec Kit files of a project from two stock installs generated in temporary directories — the installed version and the pinned one — without overwriting the team's work: a file identical to the old stock is replaced by the new stock, a missing file is added, and a file that differs from the old stock (the constitution, an edited template or skill) is kept and reported. Spec Kit's own bookkeeping (install options, integration manifests, the workflow registry) differs on every install, so it always takes the new version. Files the team added and files the new version dropped are left alone, and so is every file that is a symbolic link or lies in a linked folder: the backup does not follow links, so undo could not restore it.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Adoption.SpecKitUpgrade
member.summary: Generates stock Spec Kit installs of the installed and the pinned version with uvx in temporary directories, merges the pinned one into the project (), and installs the Lockflight preset. An installed pre-release that is not published (1.0.5.dev0) is compared with its release (1.0.5): a file that differs from that stock copy counts as customised and is kept, so the nearer base can only keep more, never overwrite more. Each stock install comes from PyPI, or from the version's GitHub tag when PyPI lacks it (); the result says which tag was used. A Spec Kit newer than the pinned version is never merged (that would be a downgrade): only the preset is installed. Without uvx, or when no stock install works, nothing is changed.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Canaries.GuardCanary
member.summary: The self-test's guard canary: an Edit of lockflight.yaml, sent through lockflight hook pre-tool-use as Claude Code sends it, must be blocked. Its harmless twin, a Write in src/, must be allowed: a guard that blocks everything would otherwise look as if it caught the canary. The engine's canary suite plants one in front of every guard rule.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Canaries.HumanOnlyCanary
member.summary: The self-test's human-only canary: approve spec, run with CLAUDECODE=1 as the agent's shell has it, must refuse before doing anything. It names a feature that does not exist, so even an approval that failed to refuse would stop at once. The engine's canary suite runs every command reserved for a person.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Canaries.LinkedEngineCanary
member.summary: The self-test's linked engine canary: a linked engine without the hash record lockflight link writes must not be trusted: doctor fails it without running it, as the hook shim refuses it. The harmless twin, the same engine with a matching record, must be trusted. Planted in the scratch project; the planted engine is never run.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Canaries.RedCanary
member.summary: The self-test's red canary: a red whose test fails by Assert.Fail must be classified RED_IN_TEST and rejected (it fails whatever the production code does). Judged as redgreen red judges a run; the harmless twin, an assertion on production code's result, must be accepted (RED_ASSERT). The engine's canary suite also runs a real red on a generated project.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Canaries.SelfTestSuite
member.summary: lockflight doctor --self-test: a few canaries that show this engine build works on this machine. The guard blocks an Edit of a protected file, a human-only command refuses inside a Claude Code session, a linked engine without its hash record is not trusted, the test gate does not PASS a failing test, and red rejects a test that fails by Assert.Fail. Each is planted in a temporary scratch project, never in the project the command is run from, and nothing is built. Exits non-zero when any canary is missed or could not judge. The full canary suite, one in front of every registered guard rule and gate step, is part of the engine's tests and runs in CI on Linux, Windows and macOS.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Docs.CodeSpanPathCheck
member.summary: Paths in inline code spans. member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Docs.CommandLineCheck

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Formatting.FormatAttribution
member.summary: Decides which format diagnostics a change introduced. A diagnostic replaces a span of the file that starts at its line and column and may run into the next lines (a whitespace span such as "trailing spaces, newline, indentation"); it belongs to the change when the replacement changes the content of a changed line. A span that differs from its replacement only in carriage returns is an end-of-line difference: it comes from how git checked the file out (core.autocrlf, .gitattributes) against .editorconfig's end_of_line, not from the change, and is never attributed. When the file or the span cannot be read, the whole file is judged (conservatively attributed at the diagnostic's line). A CHARSET diagnostic (the file's byte order mark disagrees with .editorconfig's charset) is about the whole file's encoding, which an edit inside the file does not touch: it is attributed only to a file the change adds or whose byte order mark the change adds or removes (encodingChanged), like an end-of-line difference otherwise.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Formatting.FormatAttribution.CharsetDiagnostic
member.summary: dotnet format's diagnostic for a file whose encoding (byte order mark) disagrees with .editorconfig's charset.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Formatting.FormatAttribution.SpanOf(System.String,Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Formatting.FormatDiagnostic)
member.summary: The replaced text and its replacement, from the description; null when the description or position cannot be read.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Formatting.FormatAttribution.LinesAffected(System.Int32,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: The lines whose content (ignoring carriage returns) the replacement changes. When the replacement keeps the number of line breaks, each line of the span is compared on its own, so trailing spaces on an untouched line do not implicate the changed line whose indentation the same span ends in; otherwise every line the span reaches counts. Empty for an end-of-line-only difference.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Formatting.FormatAttribution.Unescape(System.String)
member.summary: dotnet format writes whitespace in descriptions as \r, \n, \t and \s (a space).

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Formatting.FormatAttribution.Replace
member.remarks:
Pattern:
Replace (?<count>\\d+) characters? with '(?<with>.*)'
Explanation:
○ Match the string "Replace ".
○ "count" capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match the string " character".
○ Match 's' atomically, optionally.
○ Match the string " with '".
○ "with" capture group.
○ Match a character other than '\n' greedily any number of times.
○ Match '\''.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Formatting.FormatAttribution.Insert
member.remarks:
Pattern:
Insert '(?<with>.*)'
Explanation:
○ Match the string "Insert '".
○ "with" capture group.
○ Match a character other than '\n' greedily any number of times.
○ Match '\''.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Formatting.FormatAttribution.Delete
member.remarks:
Pattern:
Delete (?<count>\\d+) characters?
Explanation:
○ Match the string "Delete ".

○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Parsers.EngineEvidenceHashes
member.summary: Recognizes a gitleaks finding that is one of the engine's own recorded hashes. The engine writes SHA-256 digests and commit ids under file paths and names ("tests/Shop.Tests/TokenTests.cs": "<sha-256>"), which the generic API key rule reads as a key and its value. A finding is the engine's hash only when all of these hold: the rule is the generic one, the file is a red/green, approval or review record under .lockflight/features/<id>/, the whole match is one JSON name (path characters only) and its value, and that value — the secret gitleaks found — is exactly 40 or 64 lowercase hex digits. Anything else in those files (a token of a known shape, a value that is not a bare digest) stays a finding, and so does the same line in any other file.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Parsers.EngineEvidenceHashes.EvidenceFile
member.remarks:
Pattern:
(?:^|/)\\.lockflight/features/[^/]+/(?:redgreen|approvals/[^/]+|reviews/[^/]+)\\.json\\z
Explanation:
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match '/'.
○ Match the string ".lockflight/features/".
○ Match a character other than '/' atomically at least once.
○ Match '/'.
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "redgreen".
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match the string "approvals/".
○ Match a character other than '/' greedily at least once.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match the string "reviews/".
○ Match a character other than '/' greedily at least once.
○ Match the string ".json".
○ Match if at the end of the string.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Parsers.EngineEvidenceHashes.NameAndHash
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[\\w./ -]*":[ \\t]*"(?<hash>[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})"\\z
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [ \--/\w] atomically any number of times.
○ Match the string "\":".
○ Match a character in the set [\t ] atomically any number of times.
○ Match '"'.
○ "hash" capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match a lowercase hexadecimal digit exactly 40 times.
○ Match a lowercase hexadecimal digit exactly 64 times.
○ Match '"'.
○ Match if at the end of the string.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Steps.ProtectedChangesStep
member.summary: Lists the protected files a pull request changes (pr profile, with a base ref). The hooks keep the agent out of them during a session, but a commit can still reach them by other means; these changes need a human reviewer, typically via CODEOWNERS. The step reports and never fails: a person changing policy on purpose is legitimate. Paths are those under the project root (which may be a subdirectory of the repository), relative to it; a rename lists the old path too.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Steps.SecretsStep
member.summary: Secret scanning (pr profile) with gitleaks: the commits since the base ref (CI), staged and unstaged changes of tracked files, and untracked files that git does not ignore. gitleaks' dir mode takes one path and does not read .gitignore, so the untracked files (from git ls-files --others --exclude-standard) are copied under their relative paths into a temporary directory only the current user can read, and scanned there in one run; findings and .gitleaksignore fingerprints then carry repository-relative paths. Findings are accepted only through gitleaks' own .gitleaksignore, a protected path; an added inline gitleaks:allow comment — which would silence gitleaks — fails the step (in an untracked file it is also ignored by the scan). Without gitleaks the step cannot vouch for anything, so it is NOT-EARNED rather than PASS.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Steps.SecretsStep.LeaksFoundExitCode

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Steps.TestStep.JudgeVSTest(Lockflight.Cli.Processes.ProcessResult,System.Int32,Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Parsers.TrxSummary,System.Func{System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlySet{System.String}},System.String)
member.summary: VSTest's exit code says only "something failed" (1): the TRX counters decide. No executed test is NOT-EARNED (a filter or a solution without tests exits 0); a non-zero exit without a failed test means a project or test host broke, which is ERROR. A run that did not complete (a crashed test host drops its results) is ERROR and a result that timed out, was aborted or errored FAIL, both before the known-failing baseline: a baseline covers failures it can see, never results that are missing. is the filter the run applied (null for none), named when nothing ran.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Steps.TestStep.JudgeTestingPlatform(Lockflight.Cli.Processes.ProcessResult,System.String)
member.summary: Microsoft.Testing.Platform's exit code read with its summary. A success proves something only when the summary counts a test that executed (succeeded or failed): a run whose every test was skipped exits 0 too ("Zero tests ran"), and a summary without the counts says nothing, so both are NOT-EARNED. Exit 8 (zero tests) from a run in which other test applications executed tests is judged by those tests: a filter that leaves one project with nothing to run does not void the others. is the filter the run applied (null for none), named when nothing ran.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.Steps.TestStep.ExecutedAny(System.String)
member.summary: The summary counts a test that passed or failed; a summary without the succeeded figure proves no test executed.

member.summary: Why a run executed no test. A stop filter that narrowed the run comes first: one that matches nothing is the likeliest cause, and a stop gate that runs no test proves nothing.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Gates.WorkspaceGateRunner
member.summary: Runs a profile over a workspace's units. Checks that read the whole workspace's changes run once at the root — pr: policy.protected; every profile: format; pr: secrets last — and each .NET unit runs build, test and, in pr, patch coverage and dependencies in its own directory. The stop profile judges a unit whose state differs from its last PASS: uncommitted changes, a commit, a change to shared build inputs outside every unit (, committed or not), or no PASS yet. The Stop hook also skips a unit with uncommitted changes whose state matches its cached PASS; a gate run judges every unit with uncommitted changes. The edit profile runs format only. A stop-profile PASS of a unit is remembered for both. Separate repositories run in parallel, at most at a time; units of one repository run one at a time (shared projects, shared obj/). All share the run's budget. A unit that cannot run is ERROR. The run's verdict is the worst verdict of any step.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Hooks.CopyCommandTargets
member.summary: cp, mv, install, ln and rsync. The destination may be a file or a directory, so it counts as written and so does DEST/<name of each source> (also with -t DIR/--target-directory=DIR). A copy that can create a directory tree (cp -r, every mv, rsync) or whose source names are unknown ($VAR) makes the destination a tree. mv also removes its sources. A hard link (ln without -s, cp -l/--link) shares its source's content, so a later write through the link changes the source: the source counts as written (as a tree when the copy is recursive). rsync --remove-source-files deletes the files under its sources.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Hooks.Guard.GuardRules
member.summary: The PreToolUse guard: the one place its rules are registered, in order, in two stages. Once per call, on the input alone: lockdown (which, when active, replaces the engine pin check), the engine pin, the relay guard; so a stale engine or a broken test lock can never block the recovery command through an exception while facts are built. Then per root, the project and each agent worktree under it (.claude/worktrees/*, a full checkout whose copies get the same rules at their own root): human-only commands, protected paths. The first block wins. The plugin API and unknown-event checks apply to every hook event, so they stay in , ahead of all of these.

\\{(?<position>\\d+)?(?<modifier>\\.|//|/\\.|/|#|%)?\\}
Explanation:
○ Match '{'.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ "position" capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ "modifier" capture group.
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '/'.
○ Match a character in the set [./].
○ Match a character in the set [#%/].
○ Match '}'.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Hooks.PartialTargetDecisions
member.summary: Decisions on write targets that are only partly known: paths below a directory a cd moved to that cannot be followed, paths built from unknown variables, and name patterns below a directory (find DIR -name P -delete).

member.summary: A relative path after a cd that cannot be followed may lie in any directory. The rule named is the most specific one that could match (the test lock or secrets/** rather than the catch-all .lockflight/**).

A target built from a variable the guard cannot know ($X/secrets/k) is blocked only when its literal end could be a protected path; "$TMPDIR/x.log" or a bare "$FILE" are allowed (a guardrail: variables are not followed).

A file whose name holds the output of a command (logs/*.log for logs/$(date).log) is blocked when that pattern could name a protected or locked path. A .. after the computed part could lead anywhere and is blocked.
DIR/**/NAME: blocked when an existing file of that name below the directory is protected or locked.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Hooks.PipedFileListSource
member.summary: The directories a file list piped into xargs is confined to, when the command before the pipe is one that only lists files under the paths it names: grep -l/-L (any recursion) and find. A writer behind xargs then writes at most anything under those paths (a tree), which the guard can check, instead of hidden targets. Anything else, or a listing whose paths contain a substitution, stays unknown (null).

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Hooks.ProtectedTreeScan
member.summary: Whether a command that may rewrite everything under a directory could touch a path a rule protects. One scan serves one guard decision. A directory is walked only for the rules that could match below it by pattern (secrets/** never sends a walk into node_modules; **/Directory.Build.props does), the walk keeps only files whose name fits one of those rules, and the result is reused for every directory below it, so a wildcard over thousands of siblings costs one walk.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Hooks.SessionCommandRelay
member.summary: Blocks a tool call that would put an in-session human command (/lockflight:approve, /lockflight:baseline, /lockflight:reset, /lockflight:amend) in front of Claude Code as a prompt: a scheduled task, a wakeup, a message to a session, a loop, a subagent's prompt or a shell command. A prompt Claude Code starts by itself expands slash commands like a typed one and its hook payload looks the same, so the only place to stop the agent from deciding for the person in the session is the call that would queue the prompt. Tools that only read or write files are exempt, so specs and docs that mention the commands can still be edited, except on the files Claude Code reads prompts from (): every write there is blocked, by a file tool or a shell command, because a prompt can be put together across several edits.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Hooks.ShellLiteralVariables
member.summary: The variables a POSIX command line has set to plain literal text at a point of it (S=/tmp/out; cd $S), so the write scanner can replace $S and ${S} by that text. Only assignments known to run in the current shell count: a bare assignment statement or export NAME=value that is not in a pipeline or in the background; one after && holds until the and-list ends, one after || may not have run. A prefix assignment (NAME=value cmd), a reassignment to anything but literal text and unset make the name unknown again. Compound commands, function definitions, arithmetic and builtins that set variables in other ways (read, eval, source, …) stop the tracking for the rest of the command line: every variable after them is unknown, as it is without tracking. The hook's own environment is never read: a variable the command line did not set is unknown.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Hosting.HumanOnlyCommands
member.summary: Engine commands that change what the gates accept or record a human decision. Two guardrails keep them away from the agent: the PreToolUse guard blocks shell commands that invoke them, and the engine refuses to run them inside a Claude Code session (CLAUDECODE is set in every shell the agent starts). Both are guardrails, not boundaries: a determined agent can strip the variable or hide the call; signed approvals checked in CI are the boundary.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Hosting.HumanOnlyCommands.FindInWords(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String},System.Boolean)
member.summary: The reserved command (approve spec) the words of one simple command start, or null. With , a request for help is not one: the engine prints its usage for any command line with --help or -h before it parses or runs anything. That holds only when every word after the engine reaches it, so help counts only when the engine is the program itself (after variable assignments, or dotnet), never under a wrapper (find -exec, xargs, env) that may pass on fewer words.

member.summary: The engine's standard output and error as a person's terminal receives them: everything written passes through , so text from the project cannot reach the terminal as control characters or escape sequences whichever command prints it. Line ends come from the wrapped writer. The engine's own colours (Levi, the status line) are written to instead.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Hosting.TerminalText
member.summary: Makes text printable for a person: a file name, a test name, a spec line or a ledger field comes from the project, and a control character or escape sequence in it could move the cursor, rewrite a line (PASS\rFAIL), recolour or hide text, retitle the window or set the clipboard (OSC 52), so the terminal would show something other than what the engine decided. Each such character is printed visibly instead: caret notation for C0 controls and DEL (^[ for ESC), <U+XXXX> for C1 controls and the bidirectional overrides that reorder text. Line feeds, tabs and CR LF line ends stay as they are.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Init.PermissionDenyRules
member.summary: permissions.deny rules Lockflight writes into a project's .claude/settings.json: an Edit(…) rule for each protected path, so Claude Code itself refuses the built-in file tools there, before and apart from the guard. In Claude Code an Edit rule covers every built-in tool that edits files (a Write(path) rule never matches), and /path is relative to the session's primary working directory in project settings.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Init.PermissionDenyRules.LockflightParts
member.summary: The parts of .lockflight/ a rule names. Claude Code also adds Edit deny paths to the sandbox's write denials, and the commands the agent runs write evidence, the ledger and the Stop cache there, so the whole directory is not named.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Init.PermissionDenyRules.For(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String})
member.summary: One rule per protected path. A pattern with a wildcard inside it is written as it is. A plain path, or a directory (dir/**), only when it exists: Claude Code adds these rules to the sandbox's write denials, and on Linux and WSL2 the sandbox holds a denial on a missing file with an empty read-only placeholder while a command runs, which would break a build that reads global.json or Directory.Build.props. Run init again to add files created since.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Init.SandboxSettings
member.summary: The Claude Code sandbox lists Lockflight writes into a project's .claude/settings.json: sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite for the protected paths, so that while the sandbox is on the operating system refuses a shell command's write to them (macOS Seatbelt, Linux and WSL2 bubblewrap; native Windows has no sandbox), and sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite for the .NET caches outside the project, so builds keep working inside it. The sandbox itself is not switched on here: that is the developer's or the organisation's choice (/sandbox, sandbox.enabled, managed settings).

member.name: P:Lockflight.Cli.Init.SandboxSettings.DotnetCaches
member.summary: Where dotnet writes outside the project during a restore and build: the global packages folder, NuGet's HTTP and plugin caches, and the SDK's first-run and tool files. Sandboxed commands may write only the project and the temp directory.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Init.SandboxSettings.DenyWrite(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String})
member.summary: The protected paths as sandbox entries (./ is the project root in project settings), for what exists now: on Linux and WSL2 the sandbox holds a denial on a missing file by placing an empty read-only file there while a command runs, and an empty global.json or Directory.Build.props would break the build. A pattern such as **/Directory.Build.props is written as each file it matches, because Linux supports no other wildcard in these lists. Of .lockflight/ only the linked engine and the baselines are listed: evidence, the ledger and the Stop cache are written by the commands the agent runs (gate and test runs). Run init again to add files created since.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Init.SandboxSettings.Problem(System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonObject)
member.summary: Why the sandbox lists cannot be merged into: a key on the way is not an object, or a list is not a list of strings.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Ledger.CallRedaction.UrlPassword
member.remarks:
Pattern:
(?<prefix>://[^/\\s:@]*:)[^/\\s@]+@
Explanation:
○ "prefix" capture group.
○ Match the string "://".
○ Match a character in the set [^/:@\s] atomically any number of times.
○ Match ':'.
○ Match a character in the set [^/@\s] atomically at least once.
○ Match '@'.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Ledger.CallRedaction.Base64Run
member.remarks:
Pattern:
(?<![A-Za-z0-9+/_\\-])[A-Za-z0-9+/_\\-]{30,}={0,2}
Explanation:
○ Zero-width negative lookbehind.
○ Match a character in the set [+\-/-9A-Z_a-z] right-to-left.
○ Match a character in the set [+\-/-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 30 times.
○ Match '=' atomically at most 2 times.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Ledger.CallRedaction.LongToken
member.remarks:
Pattern:
[A-Za-z0-9_\\-]{24,}
Explanation:
○ Match a character in the set [\-0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically at least 24 times.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Ledger.CallRedaction.Labelled
member.remarks:
Pattern:
(?<label>(?i:bearer\\s+|(?:token|password|passwd|secret|api[_-]?key|key)\\s*[=:]\\s*|--[a-z0-9-]*(?:token|password|passwd|secret|api-?key)\\s+|\\b\\w*(?:secret_access_key|_secret|_token|_password)\\s+))\\S+
Explanation:
○ "label" capture group.
○ Match with 4 alternative expressions.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [Bb].
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a character in the set [Aa].
○ Match a character in the set [Rr].
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a character in the set [Rr].
○ Match a whitespace character atomically at least once.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.Approvals.ArtifactHash
member.summary: SHA-256 of an artifact's bytes with only two normalisations, so a checkout with core.autocrlf on Windows and one on Linux hash the same spec: leading UTF-8 BOMs are dropped (a UTF-16 or UTF-32 file with a BOM is first transcoded to UTF-8, as earlier engines read it), and CRLF and a lone CR become LF. Everything else counts as written — invalid UTF-8, U+2028, U+0085 or a form feed change the hash. For UTF-8 text this equals the hash of the decoded text with its line endings normalised, which earlier engines recorded.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.Approvals.ArtifactHash.WideEncodings
member.summary: UTF-32 before UTF-16: a UTF-32 LE mark starts with the UTF-16 LE one.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.Approvals.SessionCommandGate
member.summary: What every in-session human command (/lockflight:approve, /lockflight:baseline, /lockflight:reset, /lockflight:amend) checks the same way. The UserPromptExpansion hook fires only for a prompt that expands a slash command, never for the agent's own Skill call. The command must come from the Lockflight plugin and be typed in an interactive session a person attends. It runs in two steps: without a code the engine shows the person, and not the agent, what would be recorded, with a one-time code bound to that state (); with the code, and only while the state is unchanged, it records the decision as the terminal command does. A refusal ends with the command for a separate terminal. A guardrail: it keeps the agent, headless sessions and scheduled turns from deciding, and binds the decision to what was shown; it cannot stop something that types into the person's terminal.

^(?:[0-9]{7}-[0-9]{6}-|[0-9]{7,8}-[0-9]{6}$)

○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] exactly 7 times.
○ Match '-'.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] exactly 6 times.
○ Match '-'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] atomically at least 7 and at most 8 times.
○ Match '-'.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] exactly 6 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.RedGreen.AmendRecheck
member.summary: lockflight redgreen red after an amend: the amended tests must fail in production code again (RED_STUB or RED_ASSERT), with nothing lost or added in the suite. They are run on the cycle's red-time snapshot with the amended files laid over it, so an implementation written since the red cannot make them pass; a cycle without a snapshot re-checks them on the current tree. Then their new classification replaces the old one and their files are locked again; the rest of the cycle's evidence is kept. Otherwise the amend stays open, and its files writable.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.RedGreen.FlakyCheck
member.summary: Tells FLAKY from GREEN_BEFORE for new tests that passed on a red. The re-runs are bounded twice: at most runner invocations per red, each covering every test still unproven (not one invocation per test), and all of them inside the red's time budget (gates.timeoutSeconds, counted from the start of the red). When the budget runs out the check stops and the unproven tests keep GREEN_BEFORE. That verdict stays honest: a test that passed before the implementation existed rejects the red whether or not it is also flaky — the re-runs only choose the label, never the outcome.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.RedGreen.RedClassifier
member.summary: Classifies a new test from its pre-implementation run. A red is accepted only when the failure comes from production code: a NotImplementedException whose top stack frame is in production code (RED_STUB), or an assertion (xUnit's, or one of the assertion and mocking libraries below) in a test that calls production code (RED_ASSERT). Test code is recognised by the frame's source file under a test project, or, without symbols, by its declaring type; production code by the frame's file under a production project or its type in a production assembly. Runtime and static evidence, not proof of history: the review judges assertion quality.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.RedGreen.RedClassifier.AssertionExceptions
member.summary: The exceptions of xUnit's assertions (v2 and v3). Other Xunit.Sdk exceptions are the test framework failing the test (a throwing fixture or constructor, a timeout) or Assert.Fail, which fails whatever the production code does.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.RedGreen.RedClassifier.LibraryAssertionExceptions
member.summary: The failure exceptions of assertion and mocking libraries, checked against the packages: Xunit.Sdk.XunitException (FluentAssertions and AwesomeAssertions throw it under xUnit, and an xUnit v2 assertion in a VSTest run reports it; xUnit itself never throws it bare), Shouldly's Should… failures, the two libraries' own exception without a test framework, a failed NSubstitute Received or Received.InOrder, a failed Moq verification (or an unexpected call on a strict mock), and a failed Verify snapshot. A library's other exceptions report its misuse, not the production code.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.RedGreen.RedClassifier.AssertionLibraryFrames
member.summary: Where FluentAssertions and AwesomeAssertions throw. A VSTest run prints their failure without its exception type, so the top frame identifies it.

member.summary: The order in which one failing row decides a theory's class: the worst row wins.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.RedGreen.RedStep
member.summary: lockflight redgreen red: accepts the new tests of a cycle when they all fail in production code (RED_STUB, or RED_ASSERT in a test that calls production code), which opens the cycle and locks the test projects. A new test whose code asserts nothing is flagged assertion-free but not rejected: a test may verify by letting the production code throw (a guard clause, a validator), which a static reading of the test code cannot tell from a test that verifies nothing. An accepted red keeps a snapshot of the tree (). While the open cycle has an amend waiting, a red re-checks only the amended tests instead, on that snapshot ().
member.remarks: Each test's line is followed by why it got its class; adds the exception, the deciding stack frame with its source line, and the production call found.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.RedGreen.Snapshots.RedSnapshots
member.summary: Red-time snapshots. Before a red builds, the working tree (tracked, staged and untracked files that are not ignored, without build output) is written as a commit object through a private copy of the index, so the person's index, branch and stash stay as they are; when the red is accepted, a ref keeps it: refs/lockflight/red/<feature>/<cycle>/<commit> (the commit in the name, so linked worktrees on the same feature do not overwrite each other's). The ref is local: Lockflight never pushes it. A re-check after an amend builds this tree with the amended test files laid over it (), so an implementation written since the red cannot make the amended test pass.

member.summary: A temporary, detached git worktree of a red-time snapshot, where an amended test is built and run against the code as it was at red. member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.RedGreen.SuiteChecks
member.summary: What the test suite may not lose between the baseline and a green: no test deleted, newly skipped (Skip = "…" or a runtime Assert.Skip) or newly marked Explicit = true. Explicit tests are read from the runner's listing ("Explicit": true in -list full/json, Explicit: true in MTP's text listing) and compared with the explicit set recorded at start. Run outcomes cannot tell them apart: a normal run reports every explicit test as NotRun, whether it was always explicit or was marked explicit to dodge a failure. The listing is the runner's own view of the compiled tests, so it also sees an Explicit set through a custom attribute or a constant — which a source search would miss.
Why the open cycle cannot close: its tests not passing, other new failures, deleted tests, new skips or new explicit tests.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.RedGreen.TestCodeScanner
member.summary:
Reads a built test assembly without loading it (AOT-safe) and walks a test method's IL — and the IL of the test assembly's own methods it reaches (helpers, lambdas, local functions, async and iterator state machines, base classes). It answers two questions.
Whether the test calls production code: calls, constructs or takes a delegate to a method declared in one of the production assemblies. Static evidence that the test exercises production code; it does not prove that the failing assertion compares a value the production code produced, which the review judges.
Whether the test asserts nothing: no call into an assertion library or to an assertion-named method, and no throw. Production code is not read, so a test that relies on production code throwing looks assertion-free.

member.summary:
Reads a built test assembly without loading it (AOT-safe) and walks a test method's IL — and the IL of the test assembly's own methods it reaches (helpers, lambdas, local functions, async and iterator state machines, base classes). It answers two questions.
Whether the test calls production code: calls, constructs or takes a delegate to a method declared in one of the production assemblies. Static evidence that the test exercises production code; it does not prove that the failing assertion compares a value the production code produced, which the review judges.
Whether the test asserts nothing: no call into an assertion library or to an assertion-named method, and no throw. Production code is not read, so a test that relies on production code throwing looks assertion-free.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Lifecycle.TasksDocument
member.summary: Task lines of a Spec Kit tasks.md. A task is a test task when it sits under a ### Tests for … heading, its description starts with test wording ("Test …", "Write tests …", "Spec for …", "Cover … with tests") or it names a test file (*.spec.ts, *.test.tsx, *Tests.cs, a *.Tests/ project) without starting with "Implement" or "Make". Otherwise it is a stub task when it says stub, skeleton, NotImplementedException, or declares or scaffolds signatures; everything else is implementation. Requirement IDs count wherever they appear on the line.

Reads the session JSON on stdin, and in a Lockflight project prints Levi's face beside the last verdict from the local ledger (a Stop gate, a gate run, a review run or a guard block in the past day), or, while a code typed in the session waits for its second step, the line to type. member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Paths.UnicodeNormalization
member.summary: Unicode canonical composition (NFC) for path names. The engine runs with invariant globalization, where returns its input unchanged, yet macOS file systems open a name in either form: café typed as e + U+0301 is the same file as one with U+00E9. Both a rule and a path are composed before they are compared. Covers every canonical composition pair and Hangul syllables (); characters NFC would replace without composing (the singleton U+212B ANGSTROM SIGN, composition exclusions such as U+0958) are left as they are.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Paths.WindowsPaths.ShortNameSegment
member.remarks:
Pattern:
(^|[\\\\/])[^\\\\/~]{1,6}~\\d+([.][^\\\\/]{0,3})?($|[\\\\/])
Explanation:
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [/\\].
○ Match a character in the set [^/\\~] atomically at least 1 and at most 6 times.
○ Match '~'.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [^/\\] greedily at most 3 times.
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
○ Match a character in the set [/\\].

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Proposals.OnDiskNames
member.summary: A project-relative path spelled as the file system stores it. On a file system that ignores case (macOS, Windows), SRC/app.cs opens the same file as src/App.cs, so the patch, the protected-path rule and the check for a file named twice all use the stored name, which is the one git knows. A segment that does not exist yet is kept as typed. Unicode normalization is not compared: the engine runs without culture data, so a decomposed spelling of a composed name is kept as typed (the patch still names the path that is shown, and the file system opens it).

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Proposals.PatchBuilder
member.summary: Makes a git unified diff for one proposal with git diff --no-index over a private staging copy (a/<path>, the file now; b/<path>, the proposal), so the headers read a/<path> b/<path> relative to the project root and git apply takes it there. Bytes go through untouched: line-ending conversion is switched off, the diff is written to a file rather than decoded, and the person's diff settings (external drivers, colour, text conversion, blank-line suppression) are overridden. A new file comes from /dev/null and a deletion goes to it, which git marks as such.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Proposals.ProposeCommand
member.summary: lockflight propose <path> (--from <file> | --delete) […] — turns a change the agent may not make itself (a protected file) into one patch per file under .lockflight/local/proposals/, and prints for each whether the file is protected, whether the change is high risk, its diffstat and the git apply command for the person. It applies nothing: the person reads the patch and applies it, and the guard still blocks the agent's own git apply. Every request is checked before any patch is written, so a refused pair leaves no partial set behind.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.CSharpMask
member.summary: Blanks the parts of C# source that are not code: comments, preprocessor lines, and the contents of string and character literals (their delimiters stay). The result has the same length and line breaks as the source, so braces, semicolons and positions found in it are those of the code. It is a light scan, not a parser: unusual nesting inside interpolations may blank too little or too much, which only makes a signature listing less complete.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.EfGeneratedCode
member.summary: Whether a migration designer file or a model snapshot looks like the code EF Core generates for it, so its diff can be listed instead of shown. The file must start with the // <auto-generated /> header and, with comments, preprocessor lines and the contents of string literals blanked (), hold only: usings, a namespace, the [DbContext(typeof(…))] and [Migration("…")] attributes, one partial class (deriving from ModelSnapshot for a snapshot) with one BuildTargetModel (designer) or BuildModel (snapshot) override, and model-builder statements: calls on modelBuilder, a builder lambda's parameter (b, b1…, t, j) or the providers' builder extension classes, chained calls whose names EF's fluent API uses (Has…, Is…, With……), the enum values EF writes, and seed rows of literal values. Anything else (another member, a call on any other type, a lambda with another parameter, a statement) makes the file look hand-written, and it is shown in full. It is a light check of the shape, not a parser: a file that passes holds no code beyond model-building calls with literal arguments.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.Escalations
member.summary: Raises a minor or nit finding to major when the reviewer under-rated a violated requirement: only when its spec quote is anchored in the spec (), the quote holds an RFC 2119 MUST or SHALL (upper case, as a whole word), and its reproduction fails on the current code. marks each candidate major before the reproductions run, so it goes through the same pipeline as the reviewer's own majors (one repair within the run's budget, each build within the time limit); then keeps a reproduced one major, with its original severity, and returns every other candidate to the reviewer's severity with the reason, before the fix checks. The decision is recorded in the run file either way.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FindingLifecycle
member.summary: How tracked findings move between runs. A blocker or major finding that is confirmed or unverified opens, and stays open in every later run until its reproduction, re-run by a later review, passes (fixed) or a person dismisses it. A run that does not raise an open finding again carries it, so re-running the review never makes one disappear. Only that deterministic re-run closes a finding by itself, and a confirmed finding whose reproduction cannot run this time stays confirmed. A contested finding stays contested (with the test its fix broke) while it is open, because only new findings are fix-checked. A finding raised again with a new reproduction keeps the earlier ones, and every known reproduction has to pass before it counts as fixed, so a weaker new reproduction cannot close it.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FindingLifecycle.Carry(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Lockflight.Cli.Review.ReviewFinding},Lockflight.Cli.Review.ReviewHistory)
member.summary: The run's own findings (one per id, the most severe first) plus every open finding it did not raise again. An open finding raised again keeps the higher of its two severities (with the escalation that raised the open one, when it did), and its reproduction when the new one has none, so a reviewer that re-raises a confirmed major as minor cannot close it.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FindingLifecycle.WithEarlierReproductions(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Lockflight.Cli.Review.ReviewFinding})
member.summary: The findings followed by one check per earlier reproduction of a blocker/major finding (the finding with that reproduction), in order, so can fold the judged checks back.

member.summary: Folds the judged checks of into the findings: confirmed when any known reproduction fails, rejected only when every one passes, else unverified with the first result that is not a pass.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FindingOutcome.Rejected

member.summary: The reproduction failed, but the reviewer's own fix contradicts the change: it makes the reproduction pass and breaks one of the change's own tests, or its build fails only in the change's own test files. A person must judge it.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixCheckResult
member.summary: What happened when the engine applied a confirmed finding's fix in isolation and ran its reproduction and the change's own tests.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixCheckResult.None
member.summary: No fix check: the finding gave no fix, was not confirmed in this run, or was open from an earlier run.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixCheckResult.Held
member.summary: With the fix, the reproduction passes and every one of the change's own tests that ran passes.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixCheckResult.BreaksOwnTest
member.summary: With the fix, the reproduction passes and at least one of the change's own tests fails: the finding is contested.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixCheckResult.DidNotApply
member.summary: The fix is not a usable diff of existing non-test C# files, or its lines are not in them, also after one repair. It says the reviewer got the diff wrong, not that the finding is: the finding stays confirmed, unchecked.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixCheckResult.DidNotBuild
member.summary: The fixed code, or the reproduction against it, does not compile, also after one repair: the finding stays confirmed, unchecked.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixCheckResult.DidNotFix
member.summary: With the fix, the reproduction still fails: the fix does not show the expectation can be met, so nothing is checked.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixCheckResult.NotRun
member.summary: The fixed build did not run or did not report the reproduction (a time limit, a runner failure): nothing is checked.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixCheckResult.BreaksOwnTestBuild
member.summary: The fixed build fails, also after one repair, and every error is in one of the change's own test files: the fix changes what those tests use, so it contradicts them like and the finding is contested.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixChecks
member.summary: Checks a confirmed finding against the change's own tests, using the reviewer's own fix. The fix is applied to copies of the production files (), built with the reproduction into the review's fix folder (), and the reproduction runs with the change's own tests in its test project (). When the fix makes the reproduction pass and breaks one of those tests, the reviewer's expectation contradicts what the author's tests encode: the finding is and names the test. A fix that does not apply or build goes back to the reviewer once, within the run's budget. If it still does not, the finding stays confirmed and unchecked, because a broken diff says the reviewer got the diff wrong, not that the finding is; except when every error of the fixed build is in the change's own test files, which the fix contradicts: then it is contested and names them. A fix that holds leaves the finding confirmed and fix-checked. Anything else (the reproduction still fails, the run did not report) leaves it confirmed and unchecked, as without a fix. This is a guardrail on the reviewer's evidence, not a proof: the fix and the reproduction are both the reviewer's, and the author's tests can be wrong too. At most one check (and one repair) per finding, each build and run within the gates' time limit.

member.param: The ids of findings that may be fix-checked: new findings, not ones open from earlier runs.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.FixPatch
member.summary: Reads a reviewer's fix, a unified diff, against the working tree without writing to it. Every file it names must be an existing C# file of a non-test project inside the repository; a fix that adds, removes or renames a file, or touches test code, is refused. Hunks are matched by their lines, not by the line numbers or counts in their headers (models get those wrong): the context and removed lines must appear in the file in order after the previous hunk, exactly or apart from trailing whitespace, and the occurrence nearest the header's line wins. A file keeps its line endings.

The choice is by path only, from a fixed list: the package lock files (packages.lock.json, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock), an EF Core model snapshot (Migrations/*ModelSnapshot.cs), and a migration's designer file (Migrations/<name>.Designer.cs) when its migration <name>.cs is in the diff or the tree (the migration itself stays in the diff). member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.HiddenTextFiles
member.summary: The changed files git reports as binary although their content is text. git decides what is binary from the file's attributes before its content: a .gitattributes line such as *.cs -diff (or binary, or a diff driver set to binary) makes it print "Binary files … differ" for a text file, so the reviewer would not see the change at all. A side counts as text the way git judges it without attributes: no NUL byte in its first 8,000 bytes. The new side is read from the working tree (the diff runs against it), the old side from the base, and a file is listed when either side is text.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.ReproductionBuild
member.summary: Builds reproductions into a test project without touching its files or its build output, then runs them. The generated source and a props file live in a fresh temporary directory; the props file (passed as CustomAfterMicrosoftCommonProps) adds the source to that one project only and sends every project of the build to its own bin/lockflight-review/ and obj/lockflight-review/ (or a review's own folder, ), so the developer's sources, bin/Debug and obj/Debug stay as they were and a build the developer runs at the same time does not collide with it. The review output folders are kept between runs, so the next review builds incrementally. Analyzers are off and warnings stay warnings: a reproduction is judged by whether it compiles and fails, not by the project's style rules. For a fix check, the props file also swaps production files for their fixed copies in the temporary directory (in the project that compiles each), and the run includes the tests named to run alongside.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.Reproductions
member.summary: Confirms blocker/major findings by running the reviewer's reproduction [Fact]s: a reproduction that compiles and fails confirms the finding, one that passes rejects it, anything else leaves it unverified. Each reproduction is built in the test project nearest the cited file (), in isolation from the developer's files and build output (). All reproductions of a project are built together; compiler errors name the reproduction they are in, so a broken one is set aside and the rest are built again, and a using directive the project's files have but the generated file cannot resolve is dropped. A new finding whose reproduction does not compile gets one repair: the reviewer sees the compiler errors and the signatures of the cited code and answers with a fixed reproduction. A repaired reproduction that fails confirms the finding and replaces the first one; one that passes leaves the finding unverified (), because only the reviewer's first, unprompted test may reject a finding. Building and running reproductions executes the project's own build logic and test fixtures, like any gate run.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.ReviewBuildFolder
member.summary: The bin/ and obj/ subfolder one review builds its reproductions into. The first review of a project at a time takes the shared , kept between runs so the next review builds incrementally; it holds a lock file (in the temporary directory, named after the project root) while it builds. A review that starts while another one holds it gets a folder of its own, removed again when it is done, so two reviews never write the same output. Fix checks build into next to it, so a fixed build never leaves its production code in the reproductions' output.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.ReviewCommand
member.summary: lockflight review [--feature id] [--base ref] [--model name] [--budget usd] — the review: the engine builds the prompt from the spec and the diff, runs a read-only claude -p with a JSON schema, confirms blocker/major findings by running their reproductions (and re-runs those of findings still open from earlier runs; a new finding's reproduction that does not compile is sent back to the reviewer once, within the run's budget), raises a minor or nit finding to major when its anchored spec quote is a MUST or SHALL sentence and its reproduction fails (), and stores the run. A run counts as the review of record only when the reviewer was shown the whole diff (at most review.maxDiffCharacters; generated files are listed, not shown), with the manifest's model, budget and diff limit, against a base whose commit is the merge base of HEAD and the target branch (review.target, else origin/HEAD's branch, else main; also the default base); others are recorded and say why not. A new confirmed finding with a fix is checked against the change's own tests () and contested when its fix contradicts them. Exit 1 when an open blocker/major finding is confirmed, 5 (NOT-EARNED) when one is unverified or contested or the run is not of record, 0 otherwise. Advisory (guardrail): it runs with the developer's credentials and the agent can skip it.

member.summary: Runs a read-only claude -p with the review schema; the prompt goes through stdin. Every mode is passed explicitly, so a change of Claude Code's defaults for -p does not change the reviewer: --restricted ignores user, project and local settings (no hooks, no plugins), --safe-mode leaves out the working tree's CLAUDE.md, skills, agents and other customizations (the change under review could have rewritten them), --strict-mcp-config skips MCP servers, --tools leaves only file reads, and --permission-mode dontAsk denies anything that would ask. Bare mode (--bare) is chosen only when an API key is set, because it never reads a subscription sign-in.

member.summary: The code change since the base: the project's own diff without Lockflight's records and the specs, then — in a workspace — each unit repository's diff with its unit path in the file names, with the text files it shows as binary. External diff tools and text conversions (diff=<driver> with a textconv) are off, so the reviewer reads the content itself. Null when git fails in any of them.

Runs the reproductions of blocker/major findings, and of the minor and nit findings that may be raised to major (), when there are any and the tests build and list; otherwise blocker/major findings stay unverified, because a finding nobody could check is not a pass, and the candidates keep their severity. Then checks the fix of each new confirmed finding that has one against the change's own tests (), and says how many checks ran and how long they took.

The findings with their reproductions judged, and the test workspace and its tests when the reproductions ran; without them (nothing runnable, or the tests do not build or list), every finding as leaves it.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.ReviewPrompt

The instructions are the engine's own, compiled in; the implementing agent cannot add to them (one steering sentence from the maker made a briefed reviewer miss every defect). Everything else — the spec, the diff, the base commit's project guidance, what the engine reads from the repository for writing reproductions (test projects, signatures, a sample test) — goes into fences named with a random marker and labelled as data the reviewer must not take instructions from. is the follow-up for one reproduction that did not compile, and for one fix that did not apply or build; both answer with the same schema and fence their material the same way.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Review.SpecQuotes
member.summary: Checks a finding's spec quote against the spec: anchored when the quote, normalised, is a substring of the spec normalised the same way. Normalising makes every run of whitespace one space, trims the ends and removes Markdown emphasis and code markers: the backticks around a code span (its content is kept as written), and any run of *, _ or backticks at the edge of a word, as in **Given** or _stops_. A run inside a word (retry_count, 2*3) or between spaces (2 * 3) is not a delimiter and stays, so two texts compare equal only when they differ by such delimiters, never by a letter, a digit, punctuation or an identifier's underscore. Case and punctuation count. A quote of fewer than words is not anchored, because a word or two of a spec says nothing about which requirement is meant.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Review.SpecQuotes.Whitespace
member.remarks:
Pattern:
\\s+
Explanation:
○ Match a whitespace character atomically at least once.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Review.SpecQuotes.Delimiters
member.remarks:
Pattern:
(?<ticks>`+)(?<code>[^`]+?)\\k<ticks>|(?<![\\p{L}\\p{N}])[*_`]+(?=\\S)|(?<=\\S)[*_`]+(?![\\p{L}\\p{N}])
Explanation:
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ "ticks" capture group.
○ Match '`' atomically at least once.
○ "code" capture group.
○ Match a character other than '`' lazily at least once.
○ Match the same text as matched by the "ticks" capture group.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Zero-width negative lookbehind.
○ Match a character in the set [\p{L}\p{N}] right-to-left.
○ Match a character in the set [*_`] greedily at least once.
○ Zero-width positive lookahead.
○ Match any character other than a whitespace character.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Zero-width positive lookbehind.
○ Match any character other than a whitespace character right-to-left.
○ Match a character in the set [*_`] greedily at least once.
○ Zero-width negative lookahead.
○ Match a character in the set [\p{L}\p{N}].

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Rules.RuleExtraction
member.summary: Finds the rules in an instruction file, deterministically. Wrapped lines are joined first: a list item runs until the next item, a blank line, a heading or a fence; a paragraph until a blank line. In a list item or table cell, a sentence with an upper-case marker (MUST, NEVER, ALWAYS, SHALL, DO NOT, REQUIRED) or a lower-case one (never, always, must, do not, don't) is a rule; in a paragraph, a sentence with an upper-case marker or starting with a lower-case one. Headings and fenced blocks are not read.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Rules.RuleStatus
member.summary: What backs a written rule. None of these is "enforced": Lockflight's local controls are guardrails, and a boundary needs a required CI check the repository cannot show.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Rules.RuleStatus.Checked
member.summary: A Lockflight guardrail refuses exactly what the rule forbids (the guard on a protected path, the human-only refusal).

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Rules.RuleStatus.GuidanceOnly

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Testing.AssemblyTestMetadata

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Testing.VSTestRunner
member.summary: Runs tests of a VSTest (xUnit v2) test assembly selected by method — dotnet test <dll> --filter "FullyQualifiedName=A|FullyQualifiedName=B" in batches — and reads the TRX: one result per executed case (theory rows included), keyed by the test definition's class and method, with each failure's exception type and first stack frame. An xUnit v2 assertion prints no exception type but a message starting Assert.Equal() Failure; it is reported as Xunit.Sdk.XunitException, the base of xUnit's assertion exceptions. A message that names neither an exception type nor an assertion (a fixture or constructor failure) has no type, so the red classifier judges it by its stack, never as an assertion.

An xUnit v2 assertion prints no exception type but a message starting Assert.Equal() Failure; it is reported as Xunit.Sdk.XunitException, the base of xUnit's assertion exceptions. member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Testing.VSTestRunner.ExceptionPrefix

Pattern:
^(?<type>(?:[A-Za-z_][\\w`]*[.+])*[A-Za-z_][\\w`]*Exception) :
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ "type" capture group.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ Match a character in the set [A-Z_a-z].
○ Match a character in the set [`\w] atomically any number of times.
○ Match a character in the set [+.].
○ Match a character in the set [A-Z_a-z].
○ Match a character in the set [`\w] greedily any number of times.
○ Match the string "Exception".
○ Match the string " : ".

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Updating.PackageUpdate
member.summary: Updates the user install from a package feed: installs the newest Lockflight.Cli into a fresh tool path, moves it to ~/.lockflight/tools/<version> and points ~/.lockflight/bin/lockflight at it as says (a link, or on Windows a copy, which replaces the old one even while that runs). The SDK runs in ~/.lockflight, outside any project, so a project's global.json pinning an SDK older than 10 (which cannot install the platform-specific package) is never in the way. Older versions stay installed: projects keep their own copies anyway.

member.name: F:Lockflight.Cli.Updating.PackageUpdateStatus.Failed

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Updating.UpdateCommand
member.summary: lockflight update, a person's command: brings Lockflight up to date in one step. An install from source pulls the checkout it was built from and reinstalls the engine and the plugin (scripts/dev-install.sh, or scripts/dev-install.ps1 on Windows); an install from a package installs the newest engine from the package feed (). Then the new engine takes over (update --project): it re-pins and links the current project and refreshes the CLAUDE.md block. The tool pin and the block are protected, so the agent cannot run this: updating the engine changes the judge.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Updating.UpdateCommand.#ctor(Lockflight.Cli.Hosting.CliContext)
member.summary: lockflight update, a person's command: brings Lockflight up to date in one step. Then the new engine takes over (update --project): it re-pins and links the current project and refreshes the CLAUDE.md block. The tool pin and the block are protected, so the agent cannot run this: updating the engine changes the judge.

member.summary: The new engine updates the project, so the pin names its own version and the block is its own text.

For a linked engine, read from the tool store folder the link finally resolves into (.store/lockflight.cli/<version>/…), else from the tools/<version> folder the link points into. member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.UnitPolicy
member.summary: The lockflight.unit.yaml a unit repository's CI judges pull requests with (vendored policy): every shell protected path that can match inside the unit, re-based (), and the gate settings with the unit's own build file and test framework. The first line names the shell commit it came from; the rest is the policy, compared by workspace sync --check.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.UnitPolicy.Body(Lockflight.Cli.Config.Manifest,Lockflight.Cli.Config.Unit)
member.summary: The policy without the header: what drift is judged on (the commit changes on every shell commit).

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.UnitPolicy.Rebase(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: A shell glob as seen from inside the unit: the globs that, matched against a path relative to the unit, protect every path the shell's glob protects there (empty when it cannot match inside the unit). The glob is read the way the guard reads it (): **/ is any number of directories, any other ** (a**b too) any characters across directories, * and ? stay within a segment. The unit's path is matched against the glob character by character; each way the glob can be part-way through when the path is used up gives what is left of it, written back as a glob — the same paths, or wider (**/ left part-way through a directory), never narrower. A glob that names the unit directory itself covers the whole unit.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.UnitPolicy.Tokens(System.String)
member.summary: The glob's tokens as the guard compiles them: every **/ first, then **, *, ? and single characters.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.UnitPolicy.Step(System.String[],System.Collections.Generic.HashSet{System.Int32},System.Char)
member.summary: The positions reached from by reading one character of the path.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.UnitPolicy.Closure(System.String[],System.Collections.Generic.HashSet{System.Int32})
member.summary: The states with every position a wildcard that may match nothing lets the path skip to.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.UnitPolicy.Skippable(System.String[],System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Whether the tokens from up to may all match nothing (the rest from is then covered).

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.UnitPolicy.BodyOf(System.String)
member.summary: A vendored file without its header line.

member.name: T:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.WorkspaceSyncCommand
member.summary: lockflight workspace sync [--check] (vendored policy): writes into every .NET unit that is its own repository what its CI needs to judge pull requests without the shell — lockflight.unit.yaml, the engine pin, the unit's baselines and the CI workflow (an edited workflow is rewritten) — all derived from the shell's protected policy, so running it never loosens anything. --check changes nothing and fails when a unit has drifted from the shell.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.WorkspaceSyncCommand.#ctor(Lockflight.Cli.Hosting.CliContext)
member.summary: lockflight workspace sync [--check] (vendored policy): writes into every .NET unit that is its own repository what its CI needs to judge pull requests without the shell — lockflight.unit.yaml, the engine pin, the unit's baselines and the CI workflow (an edited workflow is rewritten) — all derived from the shell's protected policy, so running it never loosens anything. --check changes nothing and fails when a unit has drifted from the shell.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.WorkspaceSyncCommand.Vendored(Lockflight.Cli.Config.Manifest)
member.summary: Units that get vendored policy: .NET units that are their own repository (a unit without a .NET build has no gates for its CI yet).

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.WorkspaceSyncCommand.Drift(Lockflight.Cli.Config.Manifest)
member.summary: What differs between each vendored unit and the shell's policy, without changing anything.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.WorkspaceSyncCommand.Sync(Lockflight.Cli.Config.Manifest,Lockflight.Cli.Config.Unit,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Brings one unit in line (or, with , only reports); returns what differed.

member.name: M:Lockflight.Cli.Workspace.WorkspaceSyncCommand.SyncBaselines(System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Makes the unit's baselines folder a copy of the shell's baselines for the unit; says what differed, or null. Baselines that exist only in the unit are named: they are accepted in the shell (baseline … --path <unit>), not in the unit.
